Spec 06 Graphics Demo (Godot) — semantic diff

Branch feature/godot-mvpBase 0a05959 (spec 06 plan)Head c38a544 Target main (one pull request at the end of the run)Date 2026-11-21 Commits 8Files 41 · +2356 / −332 Written by REVIEW: + CODE REVIEW: · Claude Opus 5.5

Summary

Spec 06 turns the box arena of spec 01 into a playable demo that looks like a Brawl Stars match. Play now opens a sunny 20 × 26 m canyon built in code from a pure layout (rock walls, cacti as bushes, crates, skulls and bones), with the fighter and skin chosen on home, run and attack animations and a camera that follows the fighter. The mouse, a second touch stick and a quick tap fire shots under pure combat rules (the original game's numbers); three straw dummies take hits with a health bar and “480”, break apart and come back after 5 s; the fighter turns see-through in a cactus patch; dust, a muzzle flash and sparks make it lively. No server, nothing saved; server/ and ui/ are unchanged.

  • Every statement S1–S13 has code; 224 GUT tests pass (39 new) and lint is clean. The screenshots look like the spec says.
  • Rules are pure and tested (Combat, ArenaLayout, Movement.follow); one fire() serves mouse, stick and tap.
  • A shot fired with the fighter against a wall, a rock or a dummy passes through it — out of the arena at the border (finding 1, Blocking).
  • Steps 3, 4 and 8 do not record all their checks; the browser and “5 s after Play” check of S10 is open (findings 2, 3).
  • Windowed desktop: the arena is ready in about 250 ms (was 80 ms) and stays at the 60 fps cap while running and firing.

Recommendation: Request changes. Finding 1 is Blocking (S4); it is a small fix in shot.gd with a test. Fix findings 1, 2, 4 and 6 at CLOSE; findings 3 and 5 need a plan decision.

Author Q&A

Why build the canyon in code instead of a .tscn?
D2: the layout is data (ArenaLayout), so tests check the start, the dummies and the bushes against the walls without a scene, and Canyon builds walls, cacti and decoration from the same data. MultiMeshes keep the draw calls low (S10); all art is own art (spec 03, S7).
How does a touch never fire twice?
D7: the arena reads the mouse in _unhandled_input (Back takes its click first) and ignores mouse events with DEVICE_ID_EMULATION, which Godot makes from touches; the sticks read InputEventScreenTouch. Tests push real events for both cases.
Why is the fighter see-through by swapped materials?
D11's fallback: GeometryInstance3D.transparency did nothing in the Compatibility renderer (Step 7 screenshot), so FighterModel swaps each mesh's material for a cached alpha copy.
Does the arena change anything outside it?
No server call and no save (D12); server/ and ui/ are unchanged. The home, list, fighter, info, hack and QR screens are untouched; their tests pass (224 in total).

Highlights

1 · Shot: one ray per physics frame, from where it is

What changed: Every physics frame the shot casts a ray from its position to the next one and stops at the first wall, rock or dummy, or after the range. Why it matters: This is the whole hit detection of S4 and S5; a 16 m/s shot never tunnels through a thin wall. Check: The first ray starts at the muzzle, 0.7 m in front of the fighter: next to a wall or a dummy the muzzle is already inside it and the shot passes (finding 1, record block shots).

What changed: The arena reads the left mouse button: press fires and starts holding, release stops it; motion keeps the aim point. 5 · Pure rules: release and nearest target

hack_star_godot/game/combat.gd:51-71 · 2c2b449 · Step 1 · S4 · D3

51## What releasing the aim stick does: a drag past the dead zone fires that way (unit
52## direction); a quick tap gives `Vector2.ZERO` (fire at the nearest target); anything else
53## is `NO_SHOT`.
54static func release_aim(direction: Vector2, held_seconds: float) -> Vector2:
55 if direction.length() >= AIM_DEAD_ZONE:
56 return direction.normalized()
57 if held_seconds < TAP_SECONDS:
58 return Vector2.ZERO
59 return NO_SHOTSentinel value — A special value that means 'nothing'; Vector2.INF can never be a unit direction or ZERO, so release_aim can return three outcomes in one Vector2.
60
61
62## Index of the target nearest to `from` within `max_range`, or -1.
63static func nearest_target(from: Vector2, targets: Array[Vector2], max_range: float) -> int:
64 var best: int = -1
65 var best_distance: float = max_range
66 for i: int in targets.size():
67 var distance: float = from.distance_to(targets[i])
68 if distance <= best_distance:
69 best = i
70 best_distance = distance
71 return best

What changed: release_aim folds a release into fire-this-way, fire-at-nearest (ZERO) or NO_SHOT; nearest_target returns an index or -1. Why it matters: The rules are testable without a scene (guideline: game/ has no scene access). Check: A tie in distance picks the later target (<=); harmless with three dummies.

8 · See-through in a bush by swapped materials

hack_star_godot/scenes/fighter_model.gd:245-279 · c38cd30 · Step 7 · S6 · D11

245## Makes the whole fighter see-through (in a cactus patch) or solid again.
246func set_see_through(on: bool) -> void:
247 if on == see_through:
248 return
249 see_through = on
250 if _rig != null:
251 _apply_see_through(_rig)
252
253
254## The Compatibility renderer ignores `GeometryInstance3D.transparency`, so the fighter's
255## materials are swapped for see-through copies (D11), and back.
256func _apply_see_through(node: Node) -> void:
257 for child: Node in node.get_children():
258 if child is MeshInstance3D:
259 _swap_material(child)
260 _apply_see_through(child)
261
262
263func _swap_material(mesh: MeshInstance3D) -> void:
264 if not mesh.has_meta(SOLID_META):
265 mesh.set_metaObject metadata — Stores the solid material on the mesh itself, so switching back needs no second list.(SOLID_META, mesh.material_override)
266 var solid: Material = mesh.get_meta(SOLID_META)
267 mesh.material_override = _faded(solid) if see_through else solid
268
269
270func _faded(material: Material) -> Material:
271 if not material is StandardMaterial3D:
272 return material
273 if not _faded_materials.has(material):
274 var copy: StandardMaterial3D = material.duplicate()Resource.duplicate — Copies a material; the copy gets alpha blending while the shared original stays solid for other fighters. as StandardMaterial3D
275 copy.transparency = BaseMaterial3D.TRANSPARENCY_ALPHA
276 copy.albedo_color.a *= SEE_THROUGH_ALPHA
277 copy.next_passMaterial.next_pass — A second material drawn after the first; the fighter's outline lives there and is faded too. = _faded(copy.next_pass) if copy.next_pass != null else null
278 _faded_materials[material] = copy

What changed: set_see_through swaps each mesh's material_override for a cached alpha copy (alpha 0.45) and back. Why it matters: D11's fallback: GeometryInstance3D.transparency did nothing in the Compatibility renderer (Step 7 screenshot). Check: Only material_override is swapped; the copies are cleared on setup, so a new look in a bush is faded too.

11 · Effect pools: reuse, never create

hack_star_godot/scenes/arena_effects.gd:40-50 · c38cd30 · Step 7 · S8, S10 · D10

40## Restarts the next particle node of the kind at `at` (world position) in `color`.
41func play(kind: String, at: Vector3, color: Color) -> void:
42 if not _pools.has(kind):
43 return
44 var nodes: Array = _pools[kind]
45 var particles: CPUParticles3D = nodes[_next[kind]]
46 _next[kind] = (_next[kind] + 1) % nodes.size()
47 particles.global_position = at
48 particles.color = color
49 particles.restart()CPUParticles3D.restart — Starts a one-shot emitter again from its first particle; reusing 3-4 nodes per kind avoids creating nodes every frame on a phone.
50 particles.emitting = true

What changed: play() takes the next emitter of the kind in turn, moves it, colours it and restarts it. Why it matters: CPU particles work in the Compatibility renderer on WebGL; pools keep the cost flat (S10). Check: A fifth dust puff restarts the first one; the tests check the pools never grow.

Findings

#FindingLayerClassSeverityTarget
1Shots fired point-blank pass through walls, rocks and dummies. The first ray starts at the muzzle (shot.gd:38-43), 0.7 m in front of the fighter (fighter.tscn Muzzle); when the fighter touches a wall or a dummy the muzzle is already inside it, and intersect_ray does not report a shape the ray starts in. Probe (record block shots, screenshot point-blank-east-wall): at the east border the shot leaves the arena (ends at x 18); at the centre rock it passes and hits the dummy behind; next to a dummy it passes and the dummy keeps 2400 health. S4 (stop at walls, rocks and targets) and S5 are not met there. Fix: cast the first segment from the fighter's centre at muzzle height to the muzzle (or start the shot there), with a test at a wall and at a dummyspecspecBlockingfix now — fixed 2026-11-21
2Steps 3 and 4 have no Started: and no Done line in their Notes (Step completion protocol), and their screenshot checks (Step 3: 1280×720, 390×844, 844×390 with two fighters; Step 4: running and recoil of two fighters) are not recorded, although both are ✅ and the Stage log has their cost rowsspecspecShould-fixfix now — fixed 2026-11-21
3Step 8 is ✅ and the Definition of Done says “every Step's tasks checked”, but its browser task is unchecked: S10's “playable within 5 s after Play” and S13's browser check have no measurement in the spec (this review measured only a windowed desktop run: arena ready in 249 ms, 59.8 fps, record block arena-performance). Decide: the browser check moves to the author's play-test (a D<n>, the task marked as moved), or tools/serve_web.ps1 and a browser run at CLOSEspecspecShould-fixplan decision — D15, decided 2026-11-21
4D4 says the Muzzle is 0.9 m up; fighter.tscn has 0.6 m. Step 5's Notes explain it (the 0.7 m camera-side wall), but D4 was not updatedspecdocsNitfix now — fixed 2026-11-21
5The fighter faces the aim only for one frame while it moves: fighter.gd:26-27 sets rotation.y from input_direction every physics frame, so after fire turned it (arena.gd:120) it faces the run direction again (probe: yaw 0 → −1.571 two physics frames later) and the recoil plays sideways; D7 says the fighter “turns towards it while firing”. Decide whether the aim facing holds for the attack time (e.g. while attack_left > 0)codespecNitplan decision — D16, decided 2026-11-21
6Docs: docs/architecture.md:82 calls Combat “the arena's combat rules of spec 07 (D3)” (it is spec 06); target_dummy.gd:29 says “Meshes and materials are shared by all dummies”, but _cylinder, _box and _sphere make new meshes per dummy (only materials are cached)specdocsNitfix now — fixed 2026-11-21

Good: the rules are pure and named after the decisions (Combat, ArenaLayout, Movement.follow), so the arena script only wires input to them. One fire() serves the mouse, the stick and the tap. Shots and dummies share materials and meshes per colour, effects are pools, the canyon's many pieces are MultiMeshes — the windowed run stays at 60 fps while firing. Touch and mouse are kept apart in one place (DEVICE_ID_EMULATION, _unhandled_input), with tests that push real events. The D11 fallback was found on a screenshot and written down. The Notes of Steps 2, 5 and 7 record what the screenshots showed and what was changed after them; nothing in server/ or ui/ changed, no debug output, no TODO.

Concepts glossary

_unhandled_input
Called only for events no Control consumed. Back (a Button) takes its click in the GUI pass, so a click on Back never fires.
Callable.bind
Adds arguments to a signal connection: ended(position, hit) arrives with the shot's colour appended, so the sparks match the fighter.
CollisionShape3D.disabled
Turns the shape off for physics: shots and the fighter pass the broken dummy until it respawns.
Countdown timer
A float lowered by delta each frame; when it reaches 0 the effect plays and the timer restarts at 0.25 s.
CPUParticles3D.restart
Starts a one-shot emitter again from its first particle; reusing 3-4 nodes per kind avoids creating nodes every frame on a phone.
Duck typing with has_method
The shot calls hit() on whatever it struck if it has one, so walls need no script and dummies need no common base class.
Exponential smoothing
Moves a share 1 - e^(-rate * delta) of the way each frame: the same speed at any frame rate and never past the target.
global_basis
The node's world rotation; -z of the basis is the fighter's forward, used when no dummy is in range.
global_position
The node's position in the world. Read right after rotation.y changed, Godot updates the muzzle's world transform on access, so the shot starts at the turned muzzle.
Groups
Named sets of nodes; target_dummy.tscn puts each dummy in 'targets', so the arena finds them without knowing the Dummies node.
InputEvent.DEVICE_ID_EMULATION
The device id Godot gives mouse events it makes from touches (emulate_mouse_from_touch). Ignoring them keeps one touch from both moving a stick and firing.
InputEventScreenTouch
A finger down or up with its index; the stick follows only the finger that started on it, so two sticks work at once.
intersect_ray and hit_from_inside
Returns the first shape the segment crosses, or an empty Dictionary. With hit_from_inside false (the default) a shape the ray starts inside is not reported, which is why a point-blank shot passes (finding 1).
Material.next_pass
A second material drawn after the first; the fighter's outline lives there and is faded too.
move_and_slide
Moves a CharacterBody3D by its velocity and slides along what it hits; walls, rocks and dummies (mask world + targets) stop it.
Movement.facing_yaw
The rotation around y that turns the node's forward (-z) towards a ground direction; also used by fire().
Object metadata
Stores the solid material on the mesh itself, so switching back needs no second list.
PhysicsRayQueryParameters3D
Describes one ray query: from, to and the collision mask. Here the mask 0b101 (world + targets, D13), so the fighter's own layer is never hit.
Resource.duplicate
Copies a material; the copy gets alpha blending while the shared original stays solid for other fighters.
Sentinel value
A special value that means 'nothing'; Vector2.INF can never be a unit direction or ZERO, so release_aim can return three outcomes in one Vector2.
set_input_as_handled
Stops the event here, so the other stick and the arena do not see this touch.
Signals
broken and respawned let tests (and later the match of spec 07) react without polling the dummy.
Time.get_ticks_msec
Milliseconds since the engine started, unaffected by the frame rate; the cool-down compares two of these readings (Combat.can_fire).
